question: In a municipal distribution utility, what is the primary purpose of a service level target approved by senior management?
correctAnswer: It defines the standard of service the utility commits to deliver and measure
explanation: Service level targets state the service the utility promises, so performance can be tracked against a clear standard.
options: It sets the personal work schedule for each field crew member during the coming week
It defines the standard of service the utility commits to deliver and measure
It replaces the need for annual operating budgets and capital budgets entirely
It records the location of every valve, hydrant and service line in the network
optionA: It sets the personal work schedule for each field crew member during the coming week
optionB: It defines the standard of service the utility commits to deliver and measure
optionC: It replaces the need for annual operating budgets and capital budgets entirely
optionD: It records the location of every valve, hydrant and service line in the network
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Distribution Utility Management. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: Which parameters does a system wide water quality strategy typically monitor across the distribution network?
correctAnswer: Disinfectant residual, temperature, turbidity and microbiological results
explanation: A system wide strategy tracks disinfectant residual along with temperature, turbidity and microbiological results at sampling points across the network. Tracking these parameters together shows how quality changes as water moves through the system.
options: Billing totals, meter reading routes, customer arrears and payment plan counts
Disinfectant residual, temperature, turbidity and microbiological results
Hydrant painting dates, paving schedules, main break counts and snow clearing
Pump run hours, fuel consumption, vehicle mileage and spare parts inventory
optionA: Billing totals, meter reading routes, customer arrears and payment plan counts
optionB: Disinfectant residual, temperature, turbidity and microbiological results
optionC: Hydrant painting dates, paving schedules, main break counts and snow clearing
optionD: Pump run hours, fuel consumption, vehicle mileage and spare parts inventory
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: System Wide Water Quality Strategy. See README for source scope and limitations.
blueprintObjective: Processes: System Wide Water Quality Strategy

topic: Water Loss Strategy And Audit Leadership
question: In a standard water audit, what does non revenue water represent?
correctAnswer: Water supplied into the distribution system that does not produce billed revenue
explanation: Non revenue water is the difference between water supplied and billed authorized consumption.
options: Water supplied into the distribution system that does not produce billed revenue
Water that customers store in private tanks after it passes through their meters
Water returned to the treatment plant after a large main has been flushed clean
Water held in elevated storage at midnight on the last day of the audit period
optionA: Water supplied into the distribution system that does not produce billed revenue
optionB: Water that customers store in private tanks after it passes through their meters
optionC: Water returned to the treatment plant after a large main has been flushed clean
optionD: Water held in elevated storage at midnight on the last day of the audit period
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Water Loss Strategy And Audit Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.
blueprintObjective: General: Water Loss Strategy And Audit Leadership

question: Why does a utility divide a large distribution network into separate pressure zones?
correctAnswer: To match pressure to the elevation and demand found in each part of the system
explanation: Pressure zones let the utility serve high and low ground at suitable pressures from one network.
options: To make every customer meter in the city easier to read on the same single day
To allow each neighbourhood to choose its own water source and treatment method
To reduce the number of storage facilities the utility is required to inspect
To match pressure to the elevation and demand found in each part of the system
optionA: To make every customer meter in the city easier to read on the same single day
optionB: To allow each neighbourhood to choose its own water source and treatment method
optionC: To reduce the number of storage facilities the utility is required to inspect
optionD: To match pressure to the elevation and demand found in each part of the system
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Pressure And Storage Strategy. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What is an asset register used for in distribution asset management?
correctAnswer: It lists each asset with its age, condition, location and replacement needs
explanation: The register is the inventory that supports condition review, renewal planning and budgeting.
options: It authorizes emergency purchases when a supervisor is away from the office that day
It schedules the daily routes for meter readers and locates crews across the city
It lists each asset with its age, condition, location and replacement needs
It holds the passwords for the supervisory control system used by on call operators
optionA: It authorizes emergency purchases when a supervisor is away from the office that day
optionB: It schedules the daily routes for meter readers and locates crews across the city

question: Under the Drinking Water Quality Management Standard, what is an operational plan intended to document?
correctAnswer: The quality management system that guides how drinking water is provided safely
explanation: The operational plan documents the quality management system for the subject system.
options: The quality management system that guides how drinking water is provided safely
The daily chlorine readings taken at each sampling station during the past month
The names of customers who called the utility with taste and odour complaints
The construction drawings for the next watermain replacement project in the plan

question: What is the first step in a utility scale risk assessment for a distribution system?

options: Purchasing insurance coverage for every asset listed in the corporate asset register
Writing the public notice that will be issued after an adverse water quality incident
Setting the annual training budget for operators who work in confined space entries

question: Under Ontario Regulation 170/03, who carries responsibility for ensuring a municipal residential drinking water system meets its requirements?

The owner of the system, together with the accredited operating authority
The laboratory that analyzes the samples collected from the distribution system
The plumbing contractor who installed the service lines in the newest subdivision

A complete list of every work order closed by each crew on every day of the year

question: Why are dead end mains a focus in a system wide water quality strategy?
correctAnswer: Water can age there, losing disinfectant residual and raising complaint risk
explanation: Low turnover at dead ends lets water age, which can reduce residual and affect taste and odour.
options: Water pressure there is usually higher than anywhere else in the entire network
Meters there record consumption more accurately than meters on looped mains do
Valves there are larger and cost more to replace than valves on any other main
Water can age there, losing disinfectant residual and raising complaint risk
optionA: Water pressure there is usually higher than anywhere else in the entire network
optionB: Meters there record consumption more accurately than meters on looped mains do
optionC: Valves there are larger and cost more to replace than valves on any other main
optionD: Water can age there, losing disinfectant residual and raising complaint risk

topic: Water Loss Strategy And Audit Leadership
question: An audit shows billed consumption holding steady while system input volume keeps rising. What is the best next step for the utility lead?
correctAnswer: Break the difference into apparent and real loss components to locate the cause
explanation: Splitting the gap into components shows whether metering, theft, leakage or data handling is driving it.
options: Raise customer rates at once to recover the cost of the unexplained extra volume
Break the difference into apparent and real loss components to locate the cause
Stop all planned flushing for a year so the input volume returns to its old level
Replace every customer meter in the city before doing any further audit analysis
optionA: Raise customer rates at once to recover the cost of the unexplained extra volume
optionB: Break the difference into apparent and real loss components to locate the cause
optionC: Stop all planned flushing for a year so the input volume returns to its old level
optionD: Replace every customer meter in the city before doing any further audit analysis
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Water Loss Strategy And Audit Leadership. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: A high elevation neighbourhood reports low pressure at peak hours while a low area nearby has pressure higher than needed. What should the strategy review examine first?
correctAnswer: Zone boundaries, storage levels and pressure reducing valve settings together
explanation: Peak complaints at different elevations usually trace to how zones, storage and valves work together.
options: The colour and coating of hydrants along the streets in both neighbourhoods first
The billing software settings used to print invoices for the two areas this month
Zone boundaries, storage levels and pressure reducing valve settings together
The age of the office vehicles assigned to crews working in that part of the city
optionA: The colour and coating of hydrants along the streets in both neighbourhoods first
optionB: The billing software settings used to print invoices for the two areas this month
optionC: Zone boundaries, storage levels and pressure reducing valve settings together
optionD: The age of the office vehicles assigned to crews working in that part of the city

question: A utility has break history, age and criticality data for its cast iron mains. How should it rank mains for renewal?
correctAnswer: By likelihood of failure combined with the consequence if that main fails
explanation: Renewal ranking weighs both how likely failure is and how much harm a failure would cause.
options: By the year the main was photographed most recently for the corporate website
By how close each main runs to the public works yard where the crews are based
By the number of letters in the street name where each main happens to be buried
By likelihood of failure combined with the consequence if that main fails
optionA: By the year the main was photographed most recently for the corporate website
optionB: By how close each main runs to the public works yard where the crews are based

question: An internal audit finds that an approved flushing procedure was updated, but field crews still carry the older version. What is the correct leadership response?
correctAnswer: Remove the outdated version from use and retrain crews on the current procedure
explanation: Document control fails if superseded procedures stay in use, so the old version must be withdrawn.
options: Leave both versions in circulation so crews can choose the one they prefer to use
Remove the outdated version from use and retrain crews on the current procedure
Wait until the next external audit to see whether the auditor notices the difference
Ask each crew lead to rewrite the procedure in a form that suits their own team
optionA: Leave both versions in circulation so crews can choose the one they prefer to use
optionB: Remove the outdated version from use and retrain crews on the current procedure

question: On a utility risk matrix, one risk has moderate likelihood and severe consequence for public health. How should it be prioritized?
correctAnswer: Ahead of low consequence risks, even where their likelihood is about the same
explanation: Consequence drives priority, so a severe health outcome outranks minor risks of similar likelihood.
options: Below routine cost risks, because severe outcomes are considered too rare to plan for
At the same level as every other risk, since the matrix treats all entries equally
Ahead of low consequence risks, even where their likelihood is about the same
Only after the annual budget is closed, because risk ranking follows the fiscal year
optionA: Below routine cost risks, because severe outcomes are considered too rare to plan for
optionB: At the same level as every other risk, since the matrix treats all entries equally
optionC: Ahead of low consequence risks, even where their likelihood is about the same
optionD: Only after the annual budget is closed, because risk ranking follows the fiscal year

question: A new provincial requirement for distribution systems takes effect in nine months. What should the regulatory lead do first?
correctAnswer: Assess how the change affects current procedures and plan compliance before it applies
explanation: Early gap assessment lets the utility change procedures, training and records before the deadline.
options: Assess how the change affects current procedures and plan compliance before it applies
Wait for the first inspection under the new rule to learn what inspectors will expect
Assume existing procedures comply because the system passed its most recent inspection
Ask front line staff to interpret the new requirement individually as questions arise

optionB: Wait for the first inspection under the new rule to learn what inspectors will expect

question: A utility takes over distribution service for a neighbouring area with its own standards and records. What is the management priority in the first year?
correctAnswer: Align service standards, records and response procedures across both service areas
explanation: A merged service needs common standards and records so customers get consistent, traceable service.
options: Keep both areas fully separate so that no staff member ever works outside their home area
Replace all of the incoming area watermains in the first construction season after transfer
Align service standards, records and response procedures across both service areas
Change the incoming area water rates monthly until they match the utility winter average
optionA: Keep both areas fully separate so that no staff member ever works outside their home area
optionB: Replace all of the incoming area watermains in the first construction season after transfer
optionC: Align service standards, records and response procedures across both service areas

question: Each summer, disinfectant residual falls in the far end of one pressure zone while entry point results stay strong. What strategy response fits best?
correctAnswer: Increase turnover and review booster disinfection options for that zone in warm months
explanation: Warm weather and long travel time consume residual, so turnover and booster options target the cause.
options: Lower the sampling frequency in that zone until cooler weather returns in the autumn
Blame the entry point and request a full treatment plant upgrade for the next summer
Tell customers in that zone to run their taps for an hour before drinking the water
Increase turnover and review booster disinfection options for that zone in warm months
optionA: Lower the sampling frequency in that zone until cooler weather returns in the autumn
optionB: Blame the entry point and request a full treatment plant upgrade for the next summer
optionC: Tell customers in that zone to run their taps for an hour before drinking the water

Flushing dead end mains more often during the overnight hours each week of the year
Lowering system pressure at night across every pressure zone in the entire network
Painting meter chambers a brighter colour so readers can find them more quickly

The order in which hydrants in the zone are painted during the summer maintenance season
The wording of the notice sent to customers when the tank is taken out for inspection

The project that delivers the greater risk reduction for the funding available

correctAnswer: Model water age and residual for the new area so design can limit quality problems

Skip modelling because new pipes always deliver excellent water quality for decades
Model water age and residual for the new area so design can limit quality problems
Sample the new area monthly for a year and only then consider whether changes are needed

correctAnswer: A new leak or burst has developed and leak detection should be directed to that area
explanation: A sharp night flow rise with no demand change is a classic sign of new leakage in that district.

The district meter battery is stronger than usual and is sending extra flow readings
Storage in the area has been drained for painting and is refilling through the district meter

question: A pressure managed zone has leakage that rises with night pressure. What adjustment reduces leakage while protecting service?
correctAnswer: Lower excess night pressure while holding minimum service pressure at critical points
explanation: Leakage responds to pressure, so trimming excess night pressure cuts loss without harming service.
options: Raise night pressure so leaks become easier for residents to hear from the street
Remove the pressure reducing valves and let the zone follow the trunk main pressure
Close the zone boundary valves at night so no water enters the area until morning
Lower excess night pressure while holding minimum service pressure at critical points

question: Renewal funding covers only part of the mains identified as high risk over the next decade. What strategy is most defensible?

options: Renew mains in alphabetical order of street name until the available funding runs out
Spend the whole budget on one neighbourhood so the remaining risk is someone else problem
Cancel condition assessment, since full renewal cannot be funded in any case this decade

Each occurrence is unrelated, so the findings can be closed one by one without review

Delete the lower rated risks so the register looks shorter before the annual review
Plan for the combined storm scenario rather than treating each risk in isolation
Wait for a major storm to occur before deciding whether the risks are actually linked

Follow the binding regulation and document how the conflict was identified and resolved
Let each operating crew decide which document to follow on the day the question arises
Ignore both documents until an inspector raises the conflict during the next inspection

question: Growth is adding customers while much of the network is aging. What long range approach best balances the two pressures?

question: Analysis shows real losses are already below the economic level of leakage for this system. What spending decision follows?
correctAnswer: Shift effort toward other loss components that still offer better value to reduce
explanation: Below the economic level, further leakage spending costs more than the water it saves.
options: Shift effort toward other loss components that still offer better value to reduce
Keep expanding the leak crew until real losses reach zero across the whole network
Stop measuring night flows, since leakage no longer matters to the utility at all
Raise system pressure to use the spare capacity the leakage program has created
optionA: Shift effort toward other loss components that still offer better value to reduce
optionB: Keep expanding the leak crew until real losses reach zero across the whole network

question: A utility completes a monthly water balance. System input is 84,000 m3. Billed metered use is 61,500 m3, billed unmetered use is 3,000 m3, unbilled metered use is 1,200 m3 and unbilled unmetered use is 800 m3. Apparent losses are given as 2,500 m3. What are the real losses for the month? Round to 0 decimal places.
formula: Real losses = System input - Authorized consumption - Apparent losses
explanation: Real losses = System input - Authorized consumption - Apparent losses. Substitute the stated values: authorized consumption is 61,500 + 3,000 + 1,200 + 800 = 66,500 m3, so 84,000 - 66,500 - 2,500 = 15000 m3. Round only the final result to 0 decimal places.

question: A pressure zone currently uses 12,400 m3/day on an average day. A new development adds 850 service connections, and the planning allowance given for each connection is 0.62 m3/day. The peak day factor given for the zone is 1.8. What is the forecast peak day demand after the development connects? Round to 1 decimal place.
formula: Peak day demand = (Current demand + Added connections x Allowance per connection) x Peak day factor
explanation: Peak day demand = (Current demand + Added connections x Allowance per connection) x Peak day factor. Substitute the stated values: (12,400 + 850 x 0.62) x 1.8 = 12,927.0 x 1.8 = 23268.6 m3/day. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.

question: A growing zone has a peak day demand of 28,000 m3. The equalization storage given for planning is 0.25 of peak day demand. An emergency reserve of 9,500 m3 is also required, and 12,000 m3 of existing usable storage can be credited toward the total. How much additional storage is required? Round to 0 decimal places.
formula: Additional storage = Peak day demand x Equalization factor + Emergency reserve - Existing usable storage
explanation: Additional storage = Peak day demand x Equalization factor + Emergency reserve - Existing usable storage. Substitute the stated values: 28,000 x 0.25 + 9,500 - 12,000 = 7,000 + 9,500 - 12,000 = 4500 m3. Round only the final result to 0 decimal places.

question: A pumping fleet benchmark combines two stations for one year. The north station used 266,000 kWh to pump 700,000 m3, and the south station used 190,000 kWh to pump 500,000 m3. What is the combined fleet energy use per cubic metre pumped? Round to 2 decimal places.
correctAnswer: 0.38 kWh/m³
formula: Fleet specific energy = (Energy station 1 + Energy station 2) / (Volume station 1 + Volume station 2)
explanation: Fleet specific energy = (Energy station 1 + Energy station 2) / (Volume station 1 + Volume station 2). Substitute the stated values: (266,000 + 190,000) / (700,000 + 500,000) = 456,000 / 1,200,000 = 0.38 kWh/m³. Round only the final result to 2 decimal places.

question: During a minimum night flow study lasting 2.0 hours, a district meter records an inflow of 42 L/s. Legitimate night use in the district is given as 9 L/s, and the remaining flow is treated as leakage. What volume of water is lost to leakage during the study window? Use 3,600 seconds per hour and 1,000 L per m3. Round to 1 decimal place.
formula: Leakage volume = (Measured inflow - Legitimate night use) x Hours x 3600 / 1000
explanation: Leakage volume = (Measured inflow - Legitimate night use) x Hours x 3600 / 1000. Substitute the stated values: (42 - 9) x 2.0 x 3600 / 1000 = 33 x 7200 / 1000 = 237.6 m3. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place.

question: A zone now serves 18,500 people, and growth is expected to add 2,400 people. The planning demand given is 285 L per person per day, and a new industrial customer will add a steady 450 m3/day. What is the forecast average day demand for the zone in cubic metres per day? formula: Average day demand = (Current population + Added population) x Per capita demand / 1000 + Industrial demand

question: A variable speed retrofit is expected to cut specific energy at a booster station from 0.42 kWh/m³ to 0.35 kWh/m³. The station pumps 285,000 m3 in each of 4 quarters of the year. How much energy is saved over the full year? Round to 0 decimal places.
